name: Steel Dynamics, Inc.
moat_justification: A genuine lowest-quartile EAF cost structure, OmniSource scrap integration, a diversified value-added mix, and best-in-class through-cycle returns (13% three-year after-tax ROIC per the Q2 2026 release) — against commodity price-taking, the same EAF model at larger scale at Nucor, no switching costs or pricing power, spreads partly underwritten by tariffs, and an unproven aluminum platform.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 9 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
BUYBACK_TAILWIND: share count shrinking 7.0%/yr — already credited via the growth adjustment
BASIS_BREAK_SUSPECT: a >60% revenue jump/drop in the last 5 yrs — check for divestitures, big M&A, or restatements before trusting any CAGR
OE_VOLATILE: OE/share range over the last 5 yrs spans >3x — normalized base helps but the business is cyclical; widen bear weight
WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD: super-bull IV is 4.5x super-bear IV — uncertainty is huge; confidence should not be high
HIGH_NET_DEBT: net debt is 3.8x normalized OE — levered OE can vanish fast; stress the bear cases
one_liner: Best-in-class EAF steelmaker with a real cost advantage but no pricing power, moat 5/10 — at $251.49 (TTM owner's earnings $6.11/share, a 2.43% OE yield, into a guided record quarter) it yields a 5.04% weighted IRR with IV@15% of $50.28; it clears the 15% hurdle only at ~$50, and even the super-bull case ($107.25) stays below half today's price.
moat_for: Lowest-quartile EAF cost structure — variable scrap-based costs, flexes with demand
OmniSource vertical integration secures scrap supply and captures the recycling spread
13% three-year after-tax ROIC (Q2 2026 release) — best-in-class through-cycle returns
Diversified value-added mix: flat-rolled, long/rail, fabrication, ramping aluminum
Decade of buybacks — diluted shares 245,298,000 (2016) to 148,404,000 (2025) in the filed history
moat_against: Commodity price-taker on the steel price and the scrap spread — no pricing power or switching costs
Nucor runs the same EAF model at larger scale — the cost edge is shared, not proprietary
Earnings fell three straight years 2022–2025 as spreads compressed
Current spreads partly underwritten by Section 232 tariffs — policy, not a company asset
Aluminum platform still loss-making in ramp (Q2 2026 operating loss $33 million per company-results coverage)
